questions.q: Who used psilocybin mushrooms as a healing ritual long before Western scientists?
a: Mazatec communities in southern Mexico
Buddhist monks in the Himalayas
Indigenous tribes in the Amazon
Ancient Greek mystery cults
questions.why: Lesson one says the Mazatec Indians used the mushrooms for centuries in spiritual rituals and as a healing agent.

questions.q: What did brain imaging show about psilocybin's effect?
a: Brain regions that normally work alone start communicating
The brain shuts down most of its activity
Only the visual cortex becomes active
The brain produces less blood flow overall
questions.why: Lesson two says the scans showed separate areas becoming more integrated under psilocybin, which shapes the experience.

questions.q: In the 2016 depression study, what did participants report?
a: Most improved, and many said their depression was gone
Most felt no change in their symptoms
Most improved but relapsed within a week
Most experienced worse anxiety than before
questions.why: Lesson three reports that 80 percent improved and over 60 percent said their depression had disappeared completely.

questions.q: How do psychedelics seem to ease depression, according to participants?
a: They restore a sense of connection to the world
They block all negative memories permanently
They replace the need for any therapy
They increase serotonin levels for years
questions.why: Lesson three says patients described feeling reconnected to the world and the people in their lives.

questions.q: What does Pollan caution about picking psilocybin mushrooms yourself?
a: Only experts can tell safe ones from deadly kinds
They grow only in remote mountain areas
They lose their effect once they are dried
They are illegal to study in any country
questions.why: Lesson one warns that identifying the right mushroom takes expertise, so foraging on your own is not advised.
